strongest_objection: The map's whole form claim is that each carrier has its own moment of loss, and the fourth carrier leaks: of the four members the seriation calls work-borne and 'lost on leaving the floor', only Bosun's knowledge and Many seats are actually lost by leaving. Ladder credit is lost 'the day neighbours learn you can pay' and Expendable scout 'when you become too valuable to risk', both of which are changes in the beliefs of others that can happen while you are still on the floor, so by the map's own axis they belong with the belief-borne members or need a block of their own ('floor-borne': kept by the floor's structure and enforcement). The itinerary survives because its one defended adjacency, Bosun's knowledge to Second chair, uses the member that genuinely is work-borne, and the loop Stone's blood to Ladder credit to Many seats does not depend on the block label. Second-order problems are case-level: Ladder credit's susu is a cash instrument and so contradicts the item's own mechanism, and Stone's blood claims the poor go 'unprosecuted for the small' when the mechanism (enforcement costs more than it recovers) shields only against civil collection; criminal prosecution of the poor for small things is paid by the state and is, if anything, heavier. I tried to break the item type with a member the boundary claim excludes (the low bar) and found the exclusion criterion leaky, but the member it lets in belongs to a class the map has no axis for, which is a seed, not a rejection.

items.item: Dumb question's price: the cost of revealing that you do not know is proportional to what your chair says you should know, so the obvious question that topples a ten-year ritual can be asked cheaply only from the bottom, as the new hire's 'why do we do this?'; lost on the day you are supposed to know, and it returns at the summit, where a Nobel makes Feynman's dumb question a display of security rather than a gap, so it is dearest in the middle; not fresh eyes, which a new chief also has and which do not lower the price of confessing.
items.why: Tested as the closest neighbour of Beggar's mouth (both are 'the price of a confession scales with the chair'). They separate at the summit: the laureate's confessed ignorance can be worn as curiosity and so returns; confessed need cannot be worn as anything, so it does not. The item already carries the summit return; the discriminator it lacks is against Beggar's mouth, and I put it on that item rather than here. Modality note: the item states the summit return as fact ('it returns at the summit') while the record's boundary claim calls it a speculative reach; the record as a whole keeps the modality visible, so no repair.

items.item: Beggar's mouth: asking for help costs status, so the chair with none asks for free while the high chair cannot ask without a fall, as the ruined financier who cannot say he is broke or the attending who cannot ask the nurse; carried in the status you hold, it is lost on the first rung, and the loss kills, since the newly high lose the ask before they lose the need; not a costless probe, which offers something, but a confession, paid whether or not it is answered.
items.why: Its only discriminator is against Costless no, but its actual closest neighbour is Dumb question's price, and its second case ('the attending who cannot ask the nurse') reads as confessed ignorance, which is that neighbour's mechanism, not confessed need. Repair swaps the case for an unambiguous need and adds the summit discriminator the neighbour test produced.
items.repair: Beggar's mouth: asking for help costs status, so the chair with none asks for free while the high chair cannot ask without a fall, as the ruined financier who cannot say he is broke or the senior partner who cannot say the caseload is beyond her; carried in the status you hold, it is lost on the first rung, and the loss kills, since the newly high lose the ask before they lose the need; not a costless probe, which offers something, but a confession, paid whether or not it is answered; and not the dumb question, which the summit can wear as curiosity, since need can be worn as nothing but need.

items.item: Stone's blood: enforcement costs more than it recovers from someone with nothing seizable, so the low chair is unprosecuted for the small and uncollectible for the large, as the judgment-proof debtor or the sailor who jumps ship; carried in your holdings, it is lost at the first attachable asset, a wage or a deed, which is why the first pay rise of a rising person is also the day the creditors return; keepable only by holding nothing in your own name, which is a fraud or a vow; not the freedom to move but the immunity from being moved against.
items.why: 'Unprosecuted for the small' promotes a false generality: the stated mechanism (enforcement costs more than it recovers) governs civil collection, where the plaintiff pays; the state prosecutes the poor for small things at its own expense and often more heavily. The sailor who jumps ship is a move that costs nothing held (No hostages), not an immunity from being moved against, so it muddies the item's own discriminator. Repair restricts the shield to the civil side and swaps the case.
items.repair: Stone's blood: civil enforcement costs more than it recovers from someone with nothing seizable, so the low chair is not worth suing for the small and uncollectible for the large, as the judgment-proof debtor or the tenant whose deposit is the landlord's whole remedy; the shield is civil only, since the state prosecutes the small against the poor at its own expense; carried in your holdings, it is lost at the first attachable asset, a wage or a deed, which is why the first pay rise of a rising person is also the day the creditors return; keepable only by holding nothing in your own name, which is a fraud or a vow; not the freedom to move but the immunity from being moved against.

items.item: Ladder credit: where cash can settle, no obligation accrues, so the one who pays is owed nothing and the one who cannot pay builds credit in favours, the only credit line that survives a cash crash, as the susu among unbanked immigrants or the borrowed ladder that comes back as harvest help, and the exchange rate favours the poor, since gratitude is priced by sacrifice; carried in the known inability to pay, it is lost the day neighbours learn you can, when they stop owing and start billing; adds to obligation futures the exclusion, that cash sterilises the account; not the allies of many seats but the credit they enforce.
items.why: The susu is a rotating pool of cash: members pay in money and draw money out, enforced by the floor's exclusion. It is therefore a case of floor-enforced credit (the edge from Stone's blood) and a counterexample to this item's mechanism, that 'where cash can settle, no obligation accrues'. Repair moves the susu out of the item and into the edge label, replaces it with a favour case, and adds it as a discriminator. 'The only credit line that survives a cash crash' is kept but softened to what the mechanism actually supports.
items.repair: Ladder credit: where cash can settle, no obligation accrues, so the one who pays is owed nothing and the one who cannot pay builds credit in favours, the one credit line a cash crash does not close, as the borrowed ladder that comes back as harvest help or the neighbour who minds the children and is repaid in a roof, and the exchange rate favours the poor, since gratitude is priced by sacrifice; carried in the known inability to pay, it is lost the day neighbours learn you can, when they stop owing and start billing; adds to obligation futures the exclusion, that cash sterilises the account; not the allies of many seats but the credit they enforce, and not the susu, which is cash the floor enforces.

neighbor_test.left: Dumb question's price: the cost of revealing that you do not know is proportional to what your chair says you should know, so the obvious question that topples a ten-year ritual can be asked cheaply only from the bottom, as the new hire's 'why do we do this?'; lost on the day you are supposed to know, and it returns at the summit, where a Nobel makes Feynman's dumb question a display of security rather than a gap, so it is dearest in the middle; not fresh eyes, which a new chief also has and which do not lower the price of confessing.
neighbor_test.right: Beggar's mouth: asking for help costs status, so the chair with none asks for free while the high chair cannot ask without a fall, as the ruined financier who cannot say he is broke or the attending who cannot ask the nurse; carried in the status you hold, it is lost on the first rung, and the loss kills, since the newly high lose the ask before they lose the need; not a costless probe, which offers something, but a confession, paid whether or not it is answered.
neighbor_test.separating_case: Both are 'a confession priced by what the chair says you should have'; one confesses ignorance, the other need, and the author never puts them side by side. Separating case: the summit. A laureate can ask 'what is a Hilbert space, really?' and it reads as security, so Dumb question's price returns at the top, which the item already claims. The same laureate cannot say 'I cannot make rent' and have it read as anything but need, so Beggar's mouth does not return. The difference in what they let someone do follows: confessed ignorance can be re-worn as curiosity by a chair secure enough, confessed need cannot be re-worn at all, which is why the beggar's mouth is the member that needs a second order (the edge to Second chair) and the dumb question is not. They separate; the discriminator is added to Beggar's mouth. I also tested Stone's blood against No hostages, which the author admits share a carrier and loss moment: they separate on a 2x2 (a professor with assets in a trust is judgment-proof but cannot make the move that exposes her reputation; a broke junior with a wage is collectible but has nothing to cannibalise), passive immunity versus active freedom, so both stay.

boundary_case: The low bar: the low chair is graded on a curve, so a competent deck from the intern is a triumph and the same deck from the director is a shrug; carried in others' expectation, lost the first time you exceed it (the bar rises), keepable only by sandbagging. The map's boundary claim excludes it as an audience transfer 'the chair cannot operate', but that criterion would also exclude Fool's license, whose discount is equally others' to withdraw and which the fool operates only by speaking, as the intern operates the low bar only by performing. So the boundary claim's stated criterion is leaky. Ruling: the low bar is out, but for the reason the author gave Spent surprise in the breath-two residue, not the one in the boundary claim: it is consumed by use rather than lost by exposure, and the map's axis (where the advantage is kept) has no place for advantages that are spent by the first success. It is a nonmember of this map and a member of a map the seed below names.

seriation.note: Real endpoints (Fool's license, carried in nothing but a discount; Second chair, not kept in this order at all) and the one defended adjacency, Bosun's knowledge to Second chair, genuinely teaches: what a riser keeps depends on whether the low place is inside or outside the order they rose in. Two leaks that do not break the itinerary: (1) the 'work-borne' block is mislabeled for Ladder credit and Expendable scout, whose loss moments are belief changes above (learning you can pay; becoming too valuable), not leaving the floor; the honest label is 'floor-borne' with a split loss moment, or those two move up beside the belief-borne members. (2) Beggar's mouth sits in the holdings block as 'status you hold', but status is exactly what the belief-borne carriers are made of, and its loss moment ('the first rung') is a being-seen moment; the author's own limit admits Costless no is ambiguous and should admit this one too. Order within blocks is unexplained and reads as arbitrary, but the map claims only the between-block adjacencies.

edges.why: As written, 'the cheap question and the floor's knowledge must sit in different chairs' is false: the bosun holds the machine's state and can still ask cheaply about the captain's chart. The relation is real but is about subject, not chair: the question is dear over whatever your chair is supposed to hold, and Bosun's knowledge is exactly what the floor chair holds. The repair keeps it a dependency and keeps the riser consequence.
edges.repair_label: If the obvious question is about what your chair is supposed to hold, it is a confession, and the floor's knowledge is exactly what the floor chair holds; so the bosun asks cheaply about the chart and dearly about the valve, the new hire asks about the valve and is answered by a bosun who could not have asked it, and a riser who keeps a shift gets the knowledge back while the question about it grows dearer with every shift.

edges.why: 'The only credit anyone can extend you is favour-credit' is contradicted by the susu, group lending, and the company store: the uncollectible do get cash credit, enforced by the floor. The claim that survives is that the uncollectible get only credit the floor enforces, in whatever currency. The loop with Many seats still closes on that.
edges.repair_label: If a court can collect nothing from you, the only credit anyone can extend you is credit the floor enforces, in favours or in a susu's cash rounds, whose sanction is exclusion rather than seizure; so being uncollectible pushes you into the ladder economy rather than out of credit altogether.

edges.why: 'Only a separate order ... will carry it' is too strong: the anonymous line carries the ask with no chair at all, and the author's own example, the confessional, works by a sealed witness rather than by a low seat in a second order (it is a witness-architecture, not a second chair). The passage between levels survives once the alternative is named and shown to be disguise, which the Second chair item already says fails when known.
edges.repair_label: If the ask for help must be made by someone whose chair forbids it, it can be carried by no chair at all, the anonymous line, which is disguise and fails when known, or by a separate order in which their chair is genuinely low, the meeting, the white belt; so the second chair exists because the beggar's mouth cannot be faked inside the order that forbids it, and it fails when the orders touch.

modality_problems: Stone's blood: 'unprosecuted for the small' asserts as fact a generality the mechanism does not support (civil cost-recovery does not govern criminal prosecution); repaired.

Ladder credit: the susu case is cash, contradicting the item's 'where cash can settle, no obligation accrues'; repaired. 'The only credit line that survives a cash crash' is an analytical claim stated as fact; softened.

Dumb question's price: the summit return ('it returns at the summit') is stated in the item as fact while the boundary claim calls it a speculative reach; tolerable because the record's mode field and limits carry the modality, but a reader of the item alone does not see it.

Small change: 'which is why a fall from a high chair goes past the floor rather than onto it' is a prediction presented as explanation; acceptable only because the near priority names it as the thing to test, and the 'overqualified' executive is a different signal (feared flight, feared demands) from a published rate, folded in loosely.

Expendable scout: 'the youngest son who emigrates' is primogeniture leaving him nothing (No hostages) more than his being sent because he is cheap; the case fits the neighbour better than the item. Not repaired, since the other two cases carry the mechanism.

Word without a move: the shop assistant who says she would not buy it is speaking against her own interest (a commission), which is a statement-against-interest mechanism, not a no-stake one; the junior's memo and the Benedictine chapter carry the item, so no repair.
duplication: none as a whole or per item. Adjacencies to name in the record: what-a-price-does 'Invoice that ends the favor' is the same cash-sterilises-obligation mechanism seen from the price's side (Ladder credit adds the low chair's exclusion from cash and the exchange rate that favours the poor); what-a-price-does 'Price as testimony' is the signal Small change rides (Small change adds the reach downward and the overshoot on falling); hinge-kinds 'Record permanence' is No file's carrier as a hinge for advice; leverage-discoveries 'The attention gate' is the assistant as a lever, where Barber's chair is the assistant as a confidant; cooperative-masks 'The humility display that baits underestimation' is the faked version of the discount Fool's license lives on.
best_unresolved_seed: A second axis the map keeps bumping into and cannot place: advantages that are spent by use rather than lost by exposure. The low bar (credit for a competent deck), Spent surprise (the under-defended first strike), and the first cold pitch that lands are all consumed by the first success, not by being seen, and No file sits exactly at the joint, since the record is what makes the spending permanent. A map of 'what the first success costs' (renewable against spent, with No file as the passage from one to the other) would hold the two members this map had to reject and the seriation leak it could not label.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after repairing three items (a civil-only shield in Stone's blood, a cash case moved out of Ladder credit, a summit discriminator added to Beggar's mouth) and three edge labels (subject-relative dumb question, floor-enforced credit in any currency, anonymity named as the alternative to a second chair); the 'work-borne' block's loss moment is noted as mislabeled for two of its four members.
